answer: In PoA, identity verification binds each claimed agent to a Wesolowski VDF requiring a prescribed chain of modular squarings, with every result depending on its predecessor. An attacker can launch many clone instances, but GPUs cannot parallelize an individual dependency chain or reduce its wall-clock delay; they only increase hardware expenditure. Consequently, every forged identity faces a strict physical time bottleneck, whether labeled nectar, orchard, or quartz.
